name: Purpley
lede: Purpley is a strong, light-leaning purple, a plain adjective form of [[purple]] from the 2010 xkcd color survey.

sections.title: A survey adjective
sections.body:
Unlike the compound names built from it, Purpley is itself a base word in the survey, just purple with the ending "-ey" in place of "-ish" [1]. It is undocumented in any dictionary or dye record outside that 2010 survey [1]. The survey went on to spin two compounds off this one, [[vestal]] and [[pinky-purple]] [1].

Its nearest named neighbor is [[bright-lavender]], 5.4 units away and almost the same color [2]. [[medium-slate-blue]] and [[bright-violet]] sit close behind, the latter lighter and more vivid [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive matches this color across even a small share of its canvas, as photographed [3]. Its chroma is high enough that a close match on an aged, varnished canvas would be unusual [3]. The absence is a property of this archive, not a claim about painting generally [3].

questions.q: Which two names did the survey build on top of "Purpley"?
True or false: "Purpley" has a documented origin outside the 2010 survey.

openers: Purpley spun off two children of its own in the same survey, Purpley Grey and Purpley Pink.
